about: T7's real documents (t7.py, mkreal.py; lane REAL-DOC-GATE 2026-10-24). target_ms: DESIGN.md 1.2, slowest supported Mac, key -> preview commit <= 20 ms p95 for keys 50 ms apart on 1,000-page documents and Infinite Descent x2. pages: the oracle's (pdflatex, TeX Live 2026, passes until the count is stable). A site's page is 0-based and only steers dl3-keys' search for a prose line of its edit file (the nearest one is taken); line + page (beamer) are exact, from the oracle's SyncTeX for the frame's \end{frame} line.

pr_gate.about: t7.py --gate hosted, the real-doc gate (Commander 2026-10-24: wall-clock ms on a shared 3-vCPU VM is noise). A letter@ key passes when the host re-typesets at most rerun_pages_max pages (DONE rerun_pages: it converged next to the edit) and spends at most to_edited_instr_m_max million engine-thread instructions from the compile's start to the edited page (DONE stages.to_edited_instr_k: the find, a revalidation's window, the restore and the typesetting; load and clock speed do not move it); whether a typing@ key is painted by its own compile is reported, not gated (machine speed and load move it: 2 of 15 were not on an M5 Pro at load 160). Where the machine has no thread PMU counters (GitHub-hosted macOS and Ubuntu VMs: perf reports instructions:u not supported, thread_selfcounts fails) the instruction budget is reported, not gated; ci.yml's real-doc-instr job gates it on a self-hosted Mac after the merge. DESIGN 1.2's 20 ms on the slowest supported Mac is about 100 M (derived 2026-10-24: 9.2 G/s on an M5 Pro, an M1 core about 1.75x slower). Main misses that, so the budget is a RATCHET at main's value (never worse), lane GATES 2026-11-01: main df75c3a20 (after #1908, #1913, #1914; before #1916, #1918) spent 324-346 M on keys 2-7 and 464 M and 472 M on key 1 (max of keys 1-7, two runs), M5 Pro, re-typesetting 3 pages a key. Lower the budget as fixes land; 100 M is the target.
